stories.title: Labor Day Lift Off 2026 — 50th Annual Balloon Festival (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: It's free, it's this weekend, and 65 hot air balloons float over Memorial Park. The 50th annual COS Labor Day Lift Off runs Sept 5–7. Launches at 7 AM, night glow in the evenings. 🎈 #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Labor Day weekend at Memorial Park: 65 balloons, USAF skydiving, live music, food vendors, and a new 5K on Sunday. It's the 50th Labor Day Lift Off in Colorado Springs — free admission for families. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
If you haven't made Labor Day plans yet — this is your sign. 🎈

The 50th annual Colorado Springs Labor Day Lift Off is happening September 5–7 at Memorial Park, and it's completely free for families. We're talking roughly 65 hot air balloons launching every morning starting at 7 AM (get there by 6:30 to grab a good spot), plus evening night glow spectacles where the balloons light up after dark — one of the most visually stunning things you can do with kids in this city.

New this year: the festival expands onto the park's north field, there's a brand-new Overlook Club with elevated seating (ticketed), special-shape balloons make their debut, and Orangetheory is hosting a 5K on Sunday morning around Prospect Lake if your family wants to make it a full morning. There'll also be USAF skydiving demos, live music, and the usual rows of food vendors.

Balloon rides are available through vendors like Rainbow Ryders — flights run 45 minutes to an hour and include a celebratory toast and flight certificate. Worth looking into if you've got older kids or want a one-of-a-kind experience this weekend.

Three days, free admission, Memorial Park. Whether you catch morning launches or the night glow, it's a September COS tradition worth making time for.

Are you making it to the Lift Off this year? 🌄
facebook.image_caption: 🎈 50th annual Labor Day Lift Off — September 5–7 at Memorial Park in Colorado Springs. FREE. 65 balloons. Morning launches at 7 AM, night glow in the evenings. It's a COS tradition.

stories.title: Colorado Springs Celebrates Imagination Library's 3 Millionth Book (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: Colorado's Imagination Library just delivered its 3 millionth book — and Governor Polis handed it out right here in Colorado Springs. 89,000+ CO kids now get a free book every month. You can enroll your child at no cost. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Colorado's Imagination Library hit 3 million books — and Gov. Polis handed the milestone copy out in Colorado Springs. 89,000+ CO kids get a free book monthly. Enroll yours for free. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 2-3
x_posts.text: The Imagination Library now reaches 26% of all Colorado kids ages 0–5. Free monthly books, including new bilingual Spanish/English options. Sign up at imaginationlibrarycolorado.org #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Sometimes a number just stops you. 📚

This week, Governor Jared Polis handed out the 3 millionth book delivered to a Colorado child through the Imagination Library — and he did it right here in Colorado Springs, at the Early Connections location on Rio Grande Street.

The Imagination Library mails a free, age-appropriate book to enrolled children every single month, from birth until they start school. The program has grown to reach more than 89,000 Colorado kids — that's 26% of all children in the state ages zero to five. And new this year: bilingual Spanish/English book options are now available, with nearly 18,500 bilingual books already mailed in 2026 alone.

If your child isn't enrolled yet, it's free and takes minutes to sign up at imaginationlibrarycolorado.org. You don't need to earn a certain income or live in a specific neighborhood. You just sign up, and the books show up.

Early childhood literacy is one of those things where consistency matters more than anything else — and a book a month, every month, from birth, is exactly that kind of consistency.

Did you know about the Imagination Library before today? Is your family already enrolled? 💙
facebook.image_caption: 📚 Colorado's Imagination Library just delivered its 3 millionth free book — milestone handed out right here in Colorado Springs. 89,000+ Colorado kids get a free, age-specific book every month. Free enrollment at imaginationlibrarycolorado.org.

stories.title: D11 School of Technology — New School's First Full Year in COS (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text: Quick D11 update: District 11 students started August 12. Looking for specialized programs in Colorado Springs? D11's new School of Technology is now in its second year. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 3-2
x_posts.text: COS back-to-school reminder: D11 started Aug 12, D20 started Aug 17–18, D49 started Aug 3–4. Three districts, three timelines — hope yours is going smoothly. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
For families still getting their bearings on the new school year — here's your Colorado Springs district quick-reference:

🏫 District 11 students began August 12. D11 continues to expand specialized programming, including the Colorado Springs School of Technology now entering its second full school year. If you have a middle or high schooler interested in STEM pathways, it's worth exploring what D11 offers in that space.

District 20 (northern COS and Monument) started August 17–18 depending on grade. District 49 (east COS and Falcon) had their staggered start August 3–4.

September is a good time to get connected with your school's parent involvement structures — PTOs, school councils, and volunteer rosters tend to open up in the first few weeks. If you're new to your district or just want to know more about what's available, each district's website (d11.org, asd20.org, d49.org) has enrollment guides, program lists, and family resource pages.

Three weeks in for most families. How's it going?

stories.title: Dot Days Community Festival — September 9–11 at Pioneers Museum (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Dot Days is back Sept 9–11 in Colorado Springs — Cultural Connections, Citizen Science, and Our Place in Nature sessions for families. Great timing right at the start of fall. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Something fun coming up next week if you're looking for a way to keep the after-school momentum going. 🌿

The Dot Days Community Festival runs September 9–11 right here in Colorado Springs, with programming designed for families and kids of all ages. Sessions include Cultural Connections, Citizen Science, and Our Place in Nature — each one a different way to engage kids with the world around them in a hands-on, accessible setting.

The Colorado Springs Pioneers Museum at Boulder Park is part of the mix, and the week runs into a "We The People: Colorado at 150" lecture series on September 12 at 2 PM if you've got a history-curious kid.

It's the kind of event that doesn't require a whole day of logistics — a session here or there works perfectly. Worth putting on the calendar for next week.

Which of the three tracks sounds most interesting to your family: Cultural Connections, Citizen Science, or Our Place in Nature?

facebook.long_form:
Co Springs Mom Collective is doing something fun this month, and it sounds like a night worth clearing the calendar for. 🤠

The 3rd annual Buck-A-Roo Ball takes place September 12 at the ProRodeo Hall of Fame and Museum of the American Cowboy — a western-themed evening designed specifically for moms and their sons. Dinner, dancing, activities, and a setting that's pretty hard to beat if you want to make a real memory.

This is the kind of event that shows up on a kid's "remember when..." list years later. The ProRodeo Hall of Fame in Colorado Springs is a genuinely great venue, and a themed evening like this with built-in activities takes the pressure off — everyone just shows up, gets into the spirit of it, and has a good time.

Check Co Springs Mom Collective's social pages for ticket information and to see if spots are still available.
